ct.identity: i_sec = i_pri / N and V_burden = Rbur * |i_sec|, so the rectifier is a current source and never clips

rating.note: the peak is a pulse; dividing it by a continuous or de-rated rating is a screening ratio, not a pass/fail

limits: the cold-start deck does not save V(ocd)/V(ocm); the burden voltage here is derived from the saved I(Lr) through the ideal-transformer identity, not measured on this deck
the transfer is measured on the hotfault srprobe raw over 2-97 A (median 0.0997 V/A against a nominal 0.1000); a cold-start raw that saved the burden nodes would confirm it
below 2 A the diode drop dominates and the identity is not used; the excluded energy sits in the first ~0.4 ms where the input has not ramped
the CT model is ideal (Kct = 0.9999, no saturation, no magnetising current), so core loss and saturation are absent from this figure
the rating ladder is the candidate's simple linear ambient de-rating (Vishay p6, 70 C to 155 C); the ambient is not measured and the curve is not a junction-temperature measurement

the peak is a microsecond-scale pulse and the time above each level is a crossing time, not an I^2t or a wave-shape convolution; the vendor single/repetitive pulse charts must be applied to the real waveform before any pass/fail
the rejected 0805 (source_mpn) is kept only as the reason the rating moved; nothing here re-qualifies it
the cold-start deck runs with 10 ns max step; it answers 'does the converter traverse start-up', not a 1 ns ledger question
